name: service-opentelemetry
title: OpenTelemetry
description: Server and browser OpenTelemetry for errors, traces, metrics, logs, and named events.
docs:
## Overview

Otlp provides server telemetry infrastructure; BrowserOtlp provides browser telemetry infrastructure. BrowserWebVitals is included as an opt-in performance collection layer. Collection features and HTTP ingestion are separate layers connected through ordinary Effect dependencies.

| Layer | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `Otlp.layer` | Server exporters, resource configuration, batching and flushing; works in HTTP applications, workers and CLIs |
| `HttpApiOtlp.layer` | Browser ingestion routes and forwarding; requires Otlp |
| `BrowserOtlp.layer(options)` | Browser exporters, lifecycle flushing and optional exception capture |
| `BrowserEvents.layer(options?)` | Optional application analytics and page tracking from service-events; requires BrowserOtlp |
| `BrowserWebVitals.layer(options?)` | Optional performance collection; requires BrowserOtlp |

## Setup

Install OpenTelemetry, including the Web Vitals layer:

```bash
bunx shadcn@latest add @krak-stack/service-opentelemetry
```

Configure a collector on the server:

```dotenv
OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=my-app-api
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318
OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp
OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=otlp
OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp
```

```ts
import { Layer } from 'effect';
import { Otlp } from '@/services/opentelemetry';
import { HttpApiOtlp } from '@/services/opentelemetry/api';

const server = HttpApiOtlp.layer.pipe(Layer.provideMerge(Otlp.layer));
```

Workers and CLIs provide Otlp.layer without HTTP routes. To enrich or persist browser application events, provide `Events.ingestionLayer` to HttpApiOtlp, then provide the application layer to the result. See [Events](./service-events) for storage and identity configuration.

Mount browser telemetry in the application's Atom runtime:

```ts
import { BrowserOtlp } from '@/services/opentelemetry/browser';

const telemetry = BrowserOtlp.layer({ serviceName: 'my-app-web' });
```

Browser event export is enabled by default, but creates no page tracking, identity state or sessions. Opt into Web Vitals without installing Events:

```ts
import { BrowserWebVitals } from '@/services/opentelemetry/web-vitals';

const browser = BrowserWebVitals.layer().pipe(
  Layer.provideMerge(telemetry),
);
```

Install service-events only when application analytics are needed. Merge its collection layer with Web Vitals before providing telemetry:

```ts
import { BrowserEvents } from '@/services/events/browser';

const browser = Layer.mergeAll(
  BrowserEvents.layer(),
  BrowserWebVitals.layer(),
).pipe(Layer.provideMerge(telemetry));
```

Base browser entry points do not import web-vitals. Analytics and Web Vitals share the exporter, not their OTLP scope or privacy policy.

| Browser option | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `serviceName` | Required |
| `traces` | `{}`; includes global exception capture; false disables both |
| `events` | `{}`; false disables all event export, including analytics and Web Vitals |
| `logs`, `metrics` | false; enable independently with `{}` |
| Events batching | 30 seconds, 100 records; exportInterval/maxBatchSize/shutdownTimeout supported |
| `baseUrl` | `/api/otel` |
| `serviceVersion`, `attributes`, `headers` | Optional resource/transport metadata |

Batching is shared across event scopes. Set `events: { exportInterval: '5 seconds', maxBatchSize: 20 }` for faster application analytics delivery.

## Usage

`BrowserOtlp.event(name, properties?, options?)` and `Otlp.event` return Effects. Run browser calls inside the configured runtime. Invalid inputs fail with a schema error. Events are INFO OTLP logs with eventName and active trace/span correlation; they do not create spans or persist identity.

| Event option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `userId`, `anonymousId`, `sessionId`, `messageId` | user.id, analytics.anonymous_id, session.id, log.record.uid |
| `context` | Flat attributes |
| `timestamp` | Effect DateTime.Utc occurrence time |

Precedence: context, properties, explicit identity options, scoped log annotations. Values support strings, finite numbers, booleans and homogeneous arrays. Server actor annotations come from ActorRequired or application middleware, not AuthMiddleware alone. Client IDs are never proof of authentication.

## Browser Web Vitals

BrowserWebVitals collects document-level LCP, INP, CLS, FCP and TTFB through web-vitals and sends standard OTLP events. Package consumers import from `@krak-stack/registry/opentelemetry/web-vitals`; registry installs use `@/services/opentelemetry/web-vitals`. No SQL or application analytics service is required.

Mount the composed layer from Setup in the browser runtime. BrowserOtlp owns batching, flushing and the event exporter; Web Vitals does not create another exporter. `events: false` disables all event export. Web Vitals are generic telemetry, not application records stored in SQL.

### Privacy and lifetime

DNT/GPC disable collection by default. Use `BrowserWebVitals.layer({ respectDoNotTrack: false })` only when intentionally overriding those signals. Its privacy policy is independent of BrowserEvents' enabled/analytics settings.

Closing the layer releases its subscription. Library observers are shared and document-scoped; remounting a layer does not register another set. Unsupported metrics may be absent. These are document metrics, not SPA navigation timings. No URLs, performance entries, DOM attribution or analytics identity/page context are exported automatically.

### Event format

Events follow the [OTel browser conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/browser/browser-events/): `browser.web_vital`, scope `krakstack.events`.

| Attribute | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `browser.web_vital.name` | Lowercase lcp/inp/cls/fcp/ttfb |
| `browser.web_vital.id` | Metric-instance ID |
| `browser.web_vital.value` | OTLP double; milliseconds except unitless CLS |
| `browser.web_vital.delta` | OTLP double since previous report |
| `browser.web_vital.rating` | good/needs-improvement/poor |
| `browser.web_vital.navigation_type` | Library navigation type |

Group by resource and metric ID. Use the latest cumulative value or sum deduplicated deltas, not cumulative values. Identical callbacks are suppressed; message IDs distinguish changed values but do not guarantee collector deduplication.

## Transport

| Concern | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Browser endpoints | `/api/otel/v1/{traces,metrics,logs}` |
| Proxy | Forwards bytes; Events.ingestionLayer optionally connects application recording |
| Server logs overrides | OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_ENDPOINT / OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_HEADERS |
| OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true | Disables server export, not browser collection |
| Shutdown/page hidden | Best-effort flushing; browser uses keepalive |
| Storage/credentials | Configure collector separately; credentials remain server-side |

Generic telemetry generates no visitor/session IDs or cookies. Apply edge limits and avoid sensitive data/high-cardinality Loki labels. Message IDs provide correlation, not deduplication. Package imports: `@krak-stack/registry/opentelemetry` for Otlp; subpaths `/opentelemetry/api`, `/opentelemetry/browser` and `/opentelemetry/web-vitals` for adapters and browser layers.
